source_text: Καὶ Μαρκίωνα δὲ τὸν ἀπὸ Πόντου, ἁ ς προέφημεν, προεβάλλοντο οἱ φαῦλοι δαίμονες, ὃς ἀρνεῖσθαι μὲν τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν οὐρανίων καὶ γηΐνων ἁπάντων θεὸν καὶ τὸν προκηρυχθέντα διὰ τῶν προφητῶν Χριστὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ νῦν διδάσκει, ἄλλον δέ τινα καταγγέλλει παρὰ τὸν δημιουργὸν τῶν πάντων θεὸν καὶ ὁμοίως ἕτερον υἱόν· ᾧ πολλοὶ πεισθέντες ὁ ς μόνῳ τἀληθῆ ἐπισταμένῳ ἡμῶν καταγελῶσιν, ἀπόδειξιν μηδεμίαν περὶ ὧν λέγουσιν ἔχοντες, ἀλλὰ ἀλόγως ὡς ὑπὸ λύκου ἄρνες συνηρπασμένοι βορὰ τῶν ἀθέων δογμάτων καὶ δαιμόνων γίνονται. Οὐ γὰρ ἄλλο τι ἀγωνίζονται οἱ λεγόμενοι δαίμονες, ἢ ἀπάγειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀπὸ τοῦ ποιήσαντος θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ πρωτογόνου αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ· καὶ τοὺς μὲν τῆς γῆς μὴ ἐπαίρεσθαι δυναμένους τοῖς γηΐνοις καὶ χειροποιήτοις προσήλωσαν καὶ προσηλοῦσι, τοὺς δὲ ἐπὶ θεωρίαν θείων ὁρμῶντας ὑπεκκρούοντες, ἢν μὴ λογισμὸν σώφρονα καὶ καθαρὸν καὶ ἀπαθῆ βίον ἔχωσιν, εἰς ἀσέβειαν ἐμβάλλουσιν.
pass_a_gloss: And also Marcion, the one from Pontus, whom we previously mentioned, the evil demons promoted, who denies the creator God of all heavenly and earthly things and the Christ, the Son of God, proclaimed through the prophets, and now teaches, and proclaims another besides the creator God of all and similarly another son; to whom many having been persuaded, who think they alone know the truth, mock us, having no proof concerning the things they say, but irrationally, like sheep seized by a wolf, become prey of the doctrines of the ungodly and of demons. For the so-called demons do not strive for anything else than to lead men away from the God who made them and from His firstborn Christ; and those whom they cannot lift up from the earthly and handmade things, they have attached and do attach to them, but those who are striving for a vision of divine things, they undermine, unless they have a sound and pure and passionless life, they throw them into impiety.

choices.why: meaning a state of irreverence or ungodliness

pass_b_english: Evil demons have promoted Marcion of Pontus, whom we mentioned earlier. He denies the Creator God of all things in heaven and on earth, and he denies the Christ, the Son of God, who was proclaimed through the prophets. Instead he now teaches and proclaims another god besides the Creator of all, and similarly another son. Many have been persuaded by him, though they merely imagine they alone know the truth. They mock us while offering no proof for their claims. Irrationally, like sheep seized by a wolf, they become prey to the doctrines of the ungodly and of demons. For these so-called demons strive for nothing else than to lead people away from the God who made them and from his firstborn Christ. Those whom the demons cannot lift up from earthly and handmade things they have fastened and continue to fasten to such things. But those who are striving for a vision of divine things the demons undermine; unless they possess a sound mind, a pure life, and a passionless existence, the demons throw them into impiety.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The distinction between the 'creator God' (ποιητὴν... θεὸν) and the 'other god' (ἄλλον δέ τινα... θεὸν) is preserved. The conditional clause regarding the 'sound and pure and passionless life' (λογισμὸν σώφρονα καὶ καθαρὸν καὶ ἀπαθῆ βίον) is correctly rendered in both versions. No omissions or distortions found.
